post_text:
I trusted consumer lag metrics implicitly because the monitoring dashboard stayed completely green.

When our payment settlement consumer group logged zero offset lag during peak traffic, I celebrated an efficient architecture.

We routed all billing events through a single Kafka topic, relying on thread pools to maximize JVM throughput.

The consumer offsets advanced steadily on the charts, keeping our automated alerts completely silent.

Yet, actual database writes flatlined while incoming order queues swelled.

An unhandled deserialization failure had trapped the worker threads in a silent retry loop, bypassing offset commits entirely while heartbeats kept the group alive.

The broker assumed the partition was healthy because the session didn't time out, masking dead execution paths behind green metrics.

Four hours later, thousands of customer accounts remained unbilled, leaving us with a massive manual reconciliation effort.

What I learned:

Flatline consumer lag does not prove your application is healthy; it often just means your error handling hid the failure from the broker.
lesson_extracted: Flatline consumer lag metrics do not prove health when masked processing failures hide behind valid broker heartbeats.
